Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires and players are on the field. Tazmin Brits and Laura Wolvaardt will open the batting innings for South Africa Women. Renuka Singh has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE …

Right then, that was it from the exciting first innings of the first ODI between India Women and South Africa Women. The Indians put up 265 on the board with Smriti Mandhana being the highlight of the batting innings for her brilliant century. In the bowling department, it was the experienced Ayabonga Khaka who got three wickets to her name. South Africa Women will now aim to perform better with the bat and chase down the target comfortably. The pitch does look like it could be difficult to bat on and the Indian bowlers will also plan their strategies accordingly. Grab a cup of coffee and join us in a short while for the run chase.

The centurion, Smriti Mandhana is up for a quick chat and says she wasn't aware of this being her first century in ODI's in India and she feels amazing to score that. Adds that she feels that they still need to bowl well to defend this total. Mentions that this was a two-paced track but not that bad to bat on and it is important to play every ball on its merit on such a track and they need to bowl well. Adds that she and Deepti Sharma were looking to take the game deep and minimize the dot balls and they planned to take on the bowlers after the 35th over depending on the situation and matchups. Closes by saying she was not looking to slog and controlled the temptation to swing aimlessly. Confirms that the injury is not that big and it is just a tweak that happened and a bit of rest will put things back to normal.

South Africa Women had a good start to their innings. Masabata Klaas struck early with the wicket of Shafali Verma and opened up things for the other bowlers to capitalize on. Nonkululeko Mlaba and the debutant, Annerie Dercksen gave the next two wickets to establish their stronghold on the innings. Nondumiso Shangase came through with her first wicket just when a strong partnership was forming in the middle and Ayabonga Khaka followed it up with a wicket as well putting the pressure back on the opponents. She again broke a strong partnership and gave some relief to her team. Klaas got the prized wicket of Smriti Mandhana but she had already dealt damage to them. They bowled well in the initial phases but the absence of Marizanne Kapp with the ball in hand might have affected the skipper's plans to use her bowlers. They were a bit sloppy in the field which also resulted in some extra runs being added.

India Women end their innings on 265 after losing 8 wickets. At one point they were at 99 after losing 5 of their batters. However, the partnership of Smriti Mandhana and Deepti Sharma kept them alive in this game. They started off well for a couple of overs but after Shafali Verma's dismissal the runs stopped coming and they were put under pressure. They couldn’t form strong partnerships and lost three wickets in a span of 12 overs without scoring many runs. However, Smriti Mandhana was holding one end strongly and when Jemimah Rodrigues came to bat, they formed a steady partnership. They couldn’t take it long as she was sent back in the 21st over soon followed by Richa Ghosh. Deepti Sharma turned out to be a reliable batting partner for Mandhana and they both showcased their resilience by knocking the ball around and rotating the strike. They absorbed the pressure well and made sure to keep the runs coming. They put up a strong stand and got some valuable runs for the team before Deepti Sharma was dismissed. Smriti Mandhana fought through pain and kept the runs coming. She became the first Indian batter in Women’s cricket to get two centuries against South Africa. Pooja Vastrakar and Asha Sobhana ended the innings by adding some very important runs on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the prematch formalities and it is time for the action to begin. The umpires walk out to the middle. South Africa Women discuss last-moment plans in a huddle before taking their respective positions on the field. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma jog out to open the batting innings for India Women. Ayabonga Khaka has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
The players from both teams and the match officials walk out on the ground for the national anthems. South Africa's national anthem will be followed by the national anthem of India.

South Africa Women (Playing XI) - Laura Wolvaardt (C), Tazmin Brits, Anneke Bosch, Sune Luus, Marizanne Kapp, Annerie Dercksen (On ODI Debut), Nondumiso Shangase, Sinalo Jafta (WK), Masabata Klaas, Nonkululeko Mlaba, Ayabonga Khaka.
